strategy.summary: Reproduce pandas GH#66510 (PR context: test additions mentioning iNaT sentinel INT64_MIN behavior) by exercising datetime parsing/constructor fastpaths with the specific nanosecond sentinel value that should raise OutOfBoundsDatetime, not silently become NaT. The strategy pins the behavior to the buggy revision (commit 982854070758) and a test that fails there and passes on the fixed revision, using the exact test_command that targets the added tests.

pip_packages: pytz; (optional, if required by your pandas test extras)
tzdata; (not required on non-Windows/non-Emscripten, but harmless if installed)
pinned_because: NumPy is required by pandas and is numerically relevant (timedelta is mentioned in the issue instance, but this reproduction targets the datetime iNaT sentinel parsing/constructor correctness tests). No documented NumPy version constraint was provided, so this plan leaves NumPy unpinned except to ensure a compatible build from source.
python-dateutil is listed but not numerically relevant for the datetime iNaT sentinel tests; no constraint was provided.
tzdata is listed as only required on Windows/Emscripten; no constraint was provided, so it is installed only if needed for your platform.

strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/scalar/timestamp/test_constructors.py::test_constructor_naive_datetime_renders_nat_sentinel (and optionally the tz-shift/aware-offset companion tests included in -k selection).
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy revision 982854070758, at least one selected test assertion fails because the sentinel case incorrectly produces NaT / does not raise OutOfBoundsDatetime. On the fixed revision, the selected tests pass because Timestamp(...) with the sentinel nanosecond component correctly raises OutOfBoundsDatetime with message containing the out-of-bounds nanosecond timestamp (e.g., '1677-09-21 00:12:43.145224192').
strategy.numerical_probe: Not used. This reproduction is an exception/NaT-sentinel correctness transition, not a value-inspection benchmark.

input_output_examples.buggy_output: Test fails: no OutOfBoundsDatetime is raised (or result becomes NaT indistinguishably), so the pytest raises-with-match expectation does not hold
input_output_examples.expected_output: Raises OutOfBoundsDatetime matching message "Out of bounds nanosecond timestamp: 1677-09-21 00:12:43.145224192"

risks: This strategy assumes GH#66510 is the relevant defect for the provided test diffs (the new tests all mention iNaT sentinel behavior and OutOfBoundsDatetime rejection). If your goal is specifically the timedelta sum precision regression from issue #66551, the chosen tests here will not fail for that bug.

The bug may depend on pandas compilation/feature flags affecting the fastpaths (e.g., C vs Python parser legs). These constructor tests should be stable, but the related CSV fastpath tests (parse_dates_c_fastpath_*) may vary depending on whether the C-accelerated parser is built.
Exact pass/fail on buggy vs fixed requires checking out the correct fixed commit/PR merge result; only the buggy commit hash (982854070758) was provided in the instance context.

Different platforms/architectures may affect datetime parsing codepaths; if the bug is only present under certain build configurations, you may need to ensure the C extensions are built (using editable install as specified).

oracle.reference_source: Test diffs shown in the provided evidence: asserts OutOfBoundsDatetime with match=re.escape("Out of bounds nanosecond timestamp: 1677-09-21 00:12:43.145224192").
oracle.why: The test uses pytest.raises with a regex match for the exception message; correctness is whether the exception is raised and the message names the exact out-of-bounds nanosecond timestamp.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: pytest.raises(OutOfBoundsDatetime, match=...) does not succeed: either Timestamp(..., nanosecond=192) incorrectly produces NaT (or a datetime64 value that later reads as NaT) instead of rejecting the sentinel, so no exception is raised and the test fails, or the exception message differs from the expected out-of-bounds nanosecond string.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: Timestamp(..., nanosecond=192) raises OutOfBoundsDatetime with a message matching the expected out-of-bounds nanosecond timestamp string, so tm assertions succeed.
